evals.expected_output: Detects the harness it is running inside and that harness's current model, runs preflight, prints a confirmation plan, and waits for a go-ahead before launching `bench setup run`.

Ran `./bench validate --suite agentic-all` and reported 16/16 before anything else
The proposed command includes an explicit -m <model spec> (never omitted)
The proposed command is `bench setup run`, not `bench harness run`
Defaults shown are suite agentic-hard, samples 1, concurrency 2
Stopped at the confirm gate instead of launching the suite

evals.expected_output: Skips the confirm gate, runs the named harness/model/suite detached, polls the log, then reports agent score with harness and model named.
expectations: User-supplied harness, model, suite and samples override detection

Read REPORT-live.md and surfaced its setup advice
Reported where the result JSON and report were written

expectations: Did not launch a run with --suite all
Named agentic, agentic-hard and agentic-all as the valid choices
Asked the user rather than substituting a suite on its own

expectations: Ran `./bench harness models --harness opencode` and showed the choices
Asked the user for the model instead of inventing one
Did not launch `bench setup run` without -m

evals.expected_output: Captures run conditions before launching, and the final report leads with them and appends them to REPORT-live.md.
expectations: Ran scripts/collect_context.sh before starting the suite, not after

Appended the context to this run's REPORT-live.md and said so
Did not modify a report from an earlier campaign

evals.prompt: /benchmark-harness (on a machine where another job already holds the GPU)
evals.expected_output: Surfaces the GPU contention at the confirm gate and offers to wait rather than producing an incomparable number.
expectations: Named the other GPU process and its memory use in the plan block
Explained that a contended GPU makes wall-clock and turn counts incomparable
Offered to wait instead of running silently
Still allowed the user to proceed if they chose to

evals.expected_output: Plans both arms, shows the doubled cost at the confirm gate, and after the run reports the live-vs-isolated delta beside the surface attribution.
expectations: The plan block shows arms 2 (live, isolated) and a doubled estimate
Proposed `bench setup run` for the live arm and `bench harness run` for the isolated arm
Both arms use the same -m, --suite, --samples and --concurrency
The arms are run sequentially, never concurrently
Ran scripts/surface_usage.py with --isolated and reported the delta table
Said whether the gap clears the 8-point noise floor rather than declaring a winner outright

evals.expected_output: Reports which skills and MCP servers the run actually called, not merely which were installed.
expectations: Ran scripts/surface_usage.py against this run's result JSON
Reported calls by kind (builtin / skill / mcp / plugin), not just an installed count
Stated plainly that the surface was idle when no skill or MCP call appears in the trace
Did not claim any skill or MCP server helped without a call in the trace

evals.expected_output: Reports the live arm on its own and says the A/B is missing, instead of diffing against an unrelated run.
expectations: Reported the live arm's score with its harness and model
